svg.title: Full Looped Transformer: dense, plain loop and prediction-feedback loop
svg.desc: Three panels compare dense8L, plain looping and full looping. All use an input embedding E, RMSNorm, a two-layer prelude, a middle stack and a two-layer coda. The dense model uses four distinct middle layers once. Both looped models use the same four-layer middle stack three times; passes one and three are drawn, and pass two is omitted. Plain looping carries hidden states. Full looping adds a projected expected next-token embedding to each hidden state at the same position after every pass, including the last. The inset shows RMSNorm, the tied LM head, logit softcap and fp32 softmax, then r=pE and r W_o transpose. W_o starts at zero and is shared. Validation loss and six-task zero-shot means are respectively 2.9064 and 42.53 percent for dense8L, 2.8647 and 43.77 percent for plain looping, and 2.8145 and 44.51 percent for full looping.
svg.text: tokens → Embedding E → RMSNorm → Prelude (2 layers)
Looped models: pass 2 omitted; 3 passes total. Full loop adds feedback after all 3.
